mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days when the rate falls below 2.0%.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or rank correlation between FEDFUNDS change and SPX 20d returns is <0.05 over 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.0% signals labor market weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days due to recessionary risk perception.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0%, or rank correlation between UNRATE level and SPX 5d returns is > -0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous month-over-month increases in housing starts and retail sales indicate robust consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS increase >0.5% MoM, or rank correlation between joint signal and SPX 60d returns is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, industrial production decline exceeding 0.5% month-over-month signals manufacturing weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when INDPRO declines >0.5% MoM during late-cycle expansions, or rank correlation coefficient < -0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained housing starts growth above 0.5% month-over-month reflects strong consumer confidence, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when HOUST increases >0.5% MoM, or rank correlation between HOUST change and SPX 5d returns is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.0%, or rank correlation coefficient < -0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous payroll growth >0.3% month-over-month and unemployment decline >0.1 percentage points indicate labor market strength, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when PAYEMS increases >0.3% MoM and UNRATE declines >0.1pp, or rank correlation between joint signal and SPX 60d returns is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate above 4.0% during monetary tightening cycles compresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% during monetary tightening cycles, or rank correlation coefficient < -0.05.
